title: The Host_IP column contract is hardcoded in 4 production call sites with inconsistent case sensitivity, bypassing the existing CsvManager.HostColumnName constant
existing_state: CsvManager.HostColumnName (Services/CsvManager.cs:11) is the declared single source of truth for the enforced host column, and HostGridUtilities uses it consistently with OrdinalIgnoreCase comparisons (Utilities/HostGridUtilities.cs:308, 321-322, 334-336). But the literal "Host_IP" is re-hardcoded in production code at Utilities/JobEditorValidator.cs:107, Form1.cs:2664, Form1.cs:4329, and Services/JobExecutionService.cs:494. The JobEditorValidator instance is also the only case-SENSITIVE lookup: ValidateHosts uses host.TryGetValue("Host_IP", ...) directly (JobEditorValidator.cs:107) even though the very same file defines a case-insensitive TryGetRowValue helper that it uses for the username/password columns (JobEditorValidator.cs:243-259). So the job editor's host validation applies a stricter key-matching rule than the grid code that produces and consumes those same row dictionaries — a row keyed 'host_ip' satisfies the grid utilities but fails (or sneaks past) this validator depending on direction.
recommendation: Mechanical cleanup: replace the four production literals with CsvManager.HostColumnName, and change JobEditorValidator.ValidateHosts:107 to use its own TryGetRowValue helper so Host_IP matching is case-insensitive like everywhere else. A grep for '"Host_IP"' (excluding tests) should come back empty when done.
user_benefit: Removes a latent validation inconsistency in the job editor and makes the host-column contract genuinely single-sourced, so the convention documented in CLAUDE.md ('Host_IP is the only column enforced in code') stays true as the scheduler and validators grow.

evidence.note: ValidateHosts: hardcoded literal with case-sensitive TryGetValue at :107
Case-insensitive TryGetRowValue exists in the same file but is not used for Host_IP
